title: Definition and Scope of Household Items in Baggage Rules
summary: The concept of 'household items' evolved from a broad, undefined category in early baggage rules to a more strictly regulated definition that includes weight restrictions and specific itemized lists. Over time, the legal framework shifted from general descriptions to precise, schedule-based classifications that distinguish between personal/household use and commercial imports.

evolution.definition: Shifted from a general 'reasonable quantity' standard to a specific weight-based limit of 15kg per item.
evolution.scope: Refined to exclude commercial quantities and non-personal items through explicit schedules.

timeline.change: Established the initial definition of 'baggage' including household items.
Introduced a specific weight constraint (maximum 15kg per item) for goods to qualify as baggage.

Baggage: Baggage is defined as reasonable quantities of food, clothing, household, or other personal items imported by a passenger.
Passenger: A passenger is defined as any person arriving from abroad.
Schedule: The term schedule refers to any schedule attached to these rules.

Customs Act 2023: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purpose of these rules.
Terms and expressions not defined in these rules shall carry the same meaning as attributed to them under this Act.
Unaccompanied Baggage: Unaccompanied baggage is defined as any baggage that is not brought by the passenger themselves.
Baggage: Baggage refers to food items, clothing, household items, or other personal effects imported by a passenger in reasonable quantities, provided that no single item exceeds a specified weight limit.
Passenger: A passenger is defined as any non-tourist individual arriving from abroad.
Gold Jewelry: Gold jewelry is defined as wearable and ornamental items crafted from gold of a specific karat purity or higher.

Unaccompanied Baggage: Unaccompanied baggage refers to any baggage that is not brought by the passenger themselves.
